TIL about Peter Norman, the third guy on the podium during the black power salute; 1968 Olympics. His support to the moment led to issues back in Australia, but Smith and Carlos respected him so much they were pallbearers at his funeral.

TIL the world’s richest monarch is King Maha Vajiralongkorn (Rama X) of Thailand, whose fortune is estimated at $30 billion or more. Despite ruling Thailand, he has spent much of his time living in Bavaria, Germany, where he owns lakeside property.

TIL that in 1921, the U.S. Army exhumed four unidentified WWI soldiers from cemeteries in France to randomly select one for burial at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. Their burial records were deliberately destroyed to preserve their anonymity, and the three not selected were reburied in France.
TIL that former Tsar Simeon II of Bulgaria and the current Dalai Lama are the only two people still living who were heads of state during World War II

TIL of Mary Hardy Reeser, the 1951 "Cinder Woman" whose body burned almost entirely to ash while leaving the surrounding room virtually untouched. Though popular culture blamed spontaneous human combustion, the FBI attributed her death to the "wick effect".
TIL Canada has the longest coastline in the world

TIL about the USS Tang, the submarine that sank more enemy ships (33) than any other American sub in World War II. Launched in 1943, she was sunk by her own torpedo in October 1944, killing most of her crew.
TIL that Elton John has publicly performed Candle in the Wind, 1997 (the rewritten version in tribute of Princess Diana) only once - at her funeral.

TIL that from 1980 to 2014, the Wright Amendment banned commercial flights at Dallas Love Field from flying beyond Texas and its neighboring states. The law was passed to protect DFW Airport and mainly targeted Southwest Airlines.
TIL that sturgeon isn’t considered kosher, because its scales are difficult to remove
